messages:
sarah_ledger: Heads up — vendor Karya Labs (India) just sent invoice and asked us to gross-up for local withholding (they say 10%). Can someone from tax confirm our default here? I pasted the invoice note below.

mike_taxes: tagging @taxbot and @chen_ops. Quick Qs: do we have their PAN or a tax residency cert (TRC)? Also need to know where the services were performed (IN or outside). Gross-up isn't our usual practice.

andrea_procurement: Vendor pushed this during negotiations — they want net amount preserved. If we don’t gross-up they say they'll bill a higher gross amount next time. Contract doesn't currently mandate gross-up.

sarah_ledger: invoice snippet from vendor: 
```
Invoice: KARYA-2026-204
Vendor: Karya Labs Pvt Ltd
GSTIN: 27ABCDE1234F1Z5
Amount: USD 10,000
Line: Consulting services (software integration)
Vendor note: "Please gross-up for Indian withholding tax (10%)."
```

taxbot: FYI — internal doc: India TDS on fees for technical services can vary; DTAA may reduce rates if vendor provides TRC and 10F. See internal summary: https://tax-docs.internal/dtaa/india (internal link).

chen_ops: We should ask for PAN + TRC + signed declaration about where work was done. If services performed in India, withholding may apply at source. If work performed wholly outside India, withholding may not apply — need vendor attestation.

mike_taxes: Action items: 1) Sarah ask vendor for PAN and TRC and a signed note confirming where services were performed. 2) Finance will not gross-up by default — we withhold statutory rate unless counsel authorizes gross-up / contract amendment. If vendor provides TRC and Form 10F we can consider treaty relief. We will issue Form 16A (TDS certificate) if we withhold.

sarah_ledger: Sent request to vendor at 11:09AM: asked for PAN, TRC and confirmation of service location. Will post reply here.

sarah_ledger (later): Vendor responded with TRC attached and says all work was delivered from India. They also attached a 1-paragraph request that we gross-up to avoid their local cashflow issues.

mike_taxes: With TRC + vendor resident in India, we need to check DTAA rate — could be reduced but still often requires withholding at reduced rate. I opened a ticket with external tax counsel for confirmation and a recommendation on withholding rate vs treaty claim. For now: hold payment until we receive PAN and official TRC. No gross-up without legal signoff.

chen_ops: Noted. If counsel says to withhold at statutory rate we'll proceed and provide TDS certificate. Vendor can claim credit locally.

mike_taxes: Final for now: no gross-up. We will evaluate reduced treaty rate on receipt of Form 10F/TRC and counsel memo. Sarah — please block payment and keep procurement looped. :thumbsup:

sarah_ledger: Understood — blocking payment and looping procurement. Will update when counsel responds.
